text.p: Swiss energy and engineering concern Motor-Columbus AG said that its group profit in 1996 rose to 160 million Swiss francs from 155 million in 1995.
Ordinary earnings after tax were also up 10 million Swiss francs at 150 million, it said in a statement.
Its 1996 net revenues were also higher at 1.609 billion Swiss francs versus 1.573 billion in 1995, it said.
Group earnings excluding minorities in 1996 also rose to 84 million Swiss francs from 81 million francs.
The concern's supervisory board recommended a dividend of 30 francs per share on 1996 results, unchanged from 1995.

In addition, current board member Peter Wodtke plans to step down on June 26, 1997, the date for the company's annual shareholders' meeting. Rolf Bierhoff, Jack Cizain and Ulrich Fischer were proposed as new board members.

Union Bank of Switzerland UBS is the single largest shareholder in Motor-Columbus, with a 37 percent stake, reduced after the bank said last December it would sell 40 percent of the firm. The sale comprised transfer of a 20 percent stake each to French utility Electricite de France International SA and to Germany's RWE (Rheinisch-Westfaelische Elektrizitaetswerk AG). -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
